text: 🇲🇽⚖️ Canal Once is back. The government peacefully recovered the IPN's public TV station after a two-month occupation. "We made many attempts at dialogue. None of their demands had anything to do with the channel. From the start we asked them to return the facilities — there is technology there, and above all the historical archive of Canal Once, over 70 years of content." — Mario Delgado, Secretary of Public Education Only six occupiers remained at the end. Sheinbaum: "It makes no sense that a student movement demanding improvements at the Polytechnic would hold Canal 11 for so long. The Prosecutor's Office may well look into who was paying them to be there."

🇲🇽🎨 "This is a public health problem — not a matter of self-regulation." "We face a deeply unequal relationship: families against giant companies that hold all the data, all the specialists, all the algorithm design. Collective action is needed — putting the wellbeing of children and youth before commercial interests." — Mario Delgado, Secretary of Public Education Mexico's Monday mañaneras are now a national classroom on social media and childhood — psychology, neurology, and today, platform design. Next: what Mexico will do about it.

🇲🇽⚖️ Instagram's chief, asked under oath about a teen who spent 16 hours a day on the app: "That's not addiction, that's personal choice." "When a company — like tobacco, like alcohol — knows the harms, denies them, and says its products are safe, it is the government's responsibility to protect. With young people: better to prevent than to regret." — Arturo Béjar, on the landmark Los Angeles trial against Meta His answer to the industry's "parental responsibility" line: "When you buy a toy for a child, you trust the toy is safe. Working parents don't have time to sit in the car all day to make sure it works."

🇲🇽🎨 In a single week, 1 in 5 teens receive content that makes them hate their bodies. 1 in 11 see self-harm or suicide content. "I went back to Instagram and we ran a study of 240,000 people. 1 in 5 teens get body-image-harming content in a week — some 10, over 100 times. 1 in 8 face sexual harassment, 98% from strangers. These are design choices." — Arturo Béjar, former Facebook director of user protection engineering The Mexican engineer who built Meta's protection systems broke down the six ingredients of addictive design: infinite scroll, autoplay, recommendation algorithms, notifications, popularity metrics, social pressure.

🇲🇽🎨 "In 2026, the world's democracies are starting to say: enough — not with our children." "The companies that control our children's attention used algorithms and AI to hook every child, in order to sell their attention. Then they lied about it." — Jonathan Haidt, NYU psychologist, author of The Anxious Generation Haidt addressed Mexico's mañanera by video — in Spanish — and urged two measures: phone-free schools (already in 25 US states) and 16 as the minimum age for social media accounts, following Australia's lead.

🇲🇽✊ Ñuu Tata — "the town that cares." Oaxaca is getting a three-hospital health city with 700+ beds. "In Mixtec they named it 'Ñuu Tata,' which means 'town that cares.' Three hospitals — ISSSTE, IMSS, and IMSS Bienestar — sharing services, more than 700 beds. For the first time, conceived as the Universal Health Service." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, after her weekend tour of Oaxaca The regional health city will serve all of Oaxaca and part of Puebla, with next-generation technology and every specialty. Yesterday the first stone was laid for the IMSS regional hospital in San Lorenzo Cacaotepec.

🇲🇽✊ Mexico's scholarship system: 19.6 million students. 93.7 billion pesos in the first half of 2026 alone. "If one student stays in school, a family wins. But if millions of students stay in school, the entire nation wins." — Julio León Trujillo, National Scholarship Coordinator Coverage: 14.96M in basic education, 4.16M in high school, 470K university scholarships. 2026 target: 22 million students — the largest scholarship system in the country's history. The Gertrudis Bocanegra transport scholarship expands to Zacatecas and Chiapas next cycle.

🇲🇽✊ Starting today: 6.7 million primary school students receive 2,500 pesos for supplies and uniforms. "What was promised is delivered. The President said the school-supply support would go out in August — today the dispersal of the 2,500 pesos begins." — Julio León Trujillo, National Scholarship Coordinator Deposits run August 3–14, staggered by last-name initial: 16.7 billion pesos to 6,694,988 students. 4.7 million Bienestar cards delivered (95.1%); the rest go office-by-office and door-to-door — one card was delivered to a mother who was in labor during delivery week.

🇲🇽💵 <u>REMITTANCES TO MEXICO UP 3.1% IN FIRST HALF OF 2026</u>

Remittances to Mexico reached $30.759 billion in January-June, up 3.1% year-on-year and rising for a fifth consecutive month, Banxico reported — 13 million transactions averaging $422 each (El Financiero).

Trump slapped a tax on remittances and promised mass deportations. The money Mexican families depend on keeps flowing anyway.

🇲🇽⚽ <u>PLAN KUKULKÁN: THE OPERATION THAT SECURED THE WORLD CUP</u>

Baja California is joining Plan Kukulkán, the strategy that protected the 2026 World Cup, as Governor Marina del Pilar recognized the operation that coordinated more than 124,000 federal, state and municipal personnel.

Mexico hosted the planet's biggest sporting event without a major incident — and showed, in President Sheinbaum's words, "the true face of Mexico: a country at peace and joyful."
